key_insight: High-quality biological datasets can enable strong AI models quickly, but their usefulness can fade as the underlying data changes. The paper emphasizes that AI readiness is not a one-time property — models and datasets must be continuously re-evaluated and realigned.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of keeping machine learning models accurate and relevant when biological datasets evolve over time, which can cause model-dataset mismatch and degraded performance.
method: Frames AI readiness as an ongoing process rather than a fixed label for a dataset.
Highlights the need to monitor how dataset updates affect model performance and alignment.
Encourages iterative retraining, validation, and revision of models as new data becomes available.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a reminder that strong initial performance does not guarantee long-term reliability. It supports more robust workflows for maintaining model quality in fast-changing scientific domains.
visual_elements: Timeline showing a dataset evolving over time and the model becoming misaligned
Before/after diagram comparing aligned vs. outdated model-dataset pairs
Pipeline graphic for continuous monitoring, retraining, and validation
Icon set for data quality, drift, and model refresh cycles
paper_title: Thinking and rethinking data AI readiness
